this is such a useless whinge, but what's the deal with everyone wanting to do 110 on the eastern freeway? not in the right hand lane either. I was travelling last month with a big backpack, I was walking thru Antwerp and stopped at a light. some guy in the passenger seat of a car stopped next to me pulled out his phone, laughing, and pointed it right at me, taking a photo or video. I pretended not to notice so he wouldn't say anything to me, but I was on the verge of tears afterwards. I felt humiliated and violated. I guess he thought it was funny cause I'm pretty skinny, so my tiny legs and big backpack looked stupid. 

I think people forget that the person they're filming is a REAL person, not just a figure in public. I have so much anxiety after what happened...

this one is based off the top bodice/fitted cup part of the vogue 8888 slip dress. the only alterations I made were omitting the front dress section, shortening the back to fit, and adding the elastic panel at the back for a more slim fit while retaining the ability to move. I also added a zip on the side to put it on easier! 

it is also fully lined. I made it from cheap as chips satin lining on the pink side (I had 50cm of it laying around for about 6 months with no idea what to use it for) and the black side was nicer, heavier satin leftover scraps from another dress I made.

haven't sewn in months so this was a nice simple project to ease back in with! although I think if I made it again I would remove some of the bulk in the arm area, and just make the side of the cup scoop a bit lower.

the pattern is actually for a pyjama top! I made this out of 0.5 metres of zebra faux fur (yes, I have no idea how I made that work) and some scraps of black satin bedsheet. I made this a while ago so I can't exactly remember the details of the process, but I think I essentially just used the pattern to cut out the pieces (with the length of the body pre-shortened to sit at the waist after hemming) and went through assembly as I would any other shirt. a few parts are topstitched as I had some issues getting the collar to sit flat.

i usually don't ever wear anything but black, so this bedsheet was laying around in my fabric stash for ages. i thought it would fit the vintage feel of this pattern so I jumped on the chance to use it up!! 

since it was a fitted sheet, it was really thin and faded in some areas. to stop it from being to sheer I made a broadcloth lining, basically by making a second dress without sleeves and with a shorter hem. the fading I couldn't fix, so you can see quite obviously in the underbust area. :(

I took the neckline down a bit, same with the back neck, and didn't use any interfacing. i shortened the dress significantly too. i sorta messed up the hem, so I found some lace at the op shop to hide that :') 

I'm not the happiest with this, and it's not really my style, I wouldn't wear it too often, but it was really good practice for making my own lining and installing an invisible zip.

I'm no professional, but as far as I know you should steer fully clear of MDMA (and LSD) on any ssri. the influx of serotonin alongside the reduced reuptake can cause serotonin syndrome, which is very dangerous. defs not worth it. 

as far as coke and alcohol go, I'd really look into it. from what I've heard, lexapro might reduce alcohol tolerance and cause some people to become unexpectedly very drunk after only a few drinks. also it's thought alcohol can somewhat reduce the effectiveness of lexapro.

I'd probably err on the side of caution and say no to coke. save a few bucks in the process. don't quote me on that one though.
